title: Writing E-mails
summary: E-mail (electronic mail) is a message, with text, files or pictures, sent over the internet. It is faster and cheaper than a posted letter, and distance and time zones do not matter.

Because the receiver can ask questions at once, e-mail tends to be loosely structured, like conversation. But the reader may get hundreds of messages, and the message may look different on the reader's screen, so it must be tailored to the medium.
Message header: Subject (brief, clear, telling the content; 'URGENT:' for action, 'FYI:' for information, 'Re:' for replies), From, Date, To, Reply-to, attachments.
Body: give enough context; quote the earlier mail when replying, but only what is needed; short paragraphs; lines under about 70 characters; keep the whole message to about one screen (25 lines).
Greetings and signature: usually 'Dear …' and 'Regards'/'Thanks'; a signature with name, designation and contact. Identify yourself at the top when writing to a stranger.

Never write the subject in all capitals or all small letters; discuss only non-confidential matters; avoid bad news or anger by e-mail; avoid emoticons, slang and jargon in professional mail; beware of 'Reply all'; use BCC (blind carbon copy) to hide addresses; do not reply to an old mail for a new subject.

Short forms: BRB (be right back), BTW (by the way), FYI (for your information), IMO (in my opinion), TTYL (talk to you later), TIA (thanks in advance), ASAP (as soon as possible), RSVP (please reply).

sa2: How is an e-mail different from a written letter?
An e-mail is typed and sent instantly over the internet, can carry attachments and allows quick replies; a letter is written by hand or typed, posted, and takes days to arrive.
Why is it necessary to identify yourself while writing an e-mail to someone?
The receiver may not know you. Your identity gives context — who you are, how you found them and what you want — so that the mail is read and not deleted.
Mention any four do's of writing e-mails.
Use a clear, specific subject line; address the reader properly; keep the message short and to the point; proofread before sending (also: use a polite, professional tone and a signature).
What should a good e-mail subject line be like?
Brief and clear, telling the reader what the mail is about; never in all capitals; with 'URGENT' or 'FYI' or 'Re:' where suitable.
sa3: Write an e-mail to Hotel Sunrise, Bengaluru asking them to cancel your room reservation as your travel plans have changed, and mention that you will rebook later.

To: reservations@hotelsunrise.in
Subject: Cancellation of booking no. HS2604

Dear Sir/Madam,
I had booked a deluxe room at your hotel from 12 to 14 April 2026 (booking no. HS2604). As my travel plans have changed, please cancel this reservation and refund the advance as per your policy.
I will rebook once my new dates are fixed. I regret the inconvenience.
Regards,
Arjun Mehta
98xxxxxx10
Write an e-mail to Raj Travels asking them to cancel your air tickets to Bangalore and the hotel accommodation they booked for you. You will inform them of the changed date later.

To: bookings@rajtravels.com
Subject: Cancel tickets and hotel — Bangalore trip

Dear Sir,
Please cancel my air tickets (Delhi–Bangalore, 20 May, PNR X7K2Q) and the hotel room booked for me from 20 to 23 May. Due to an urgent change in plans I cannot travel on these dates.
I will let you know the new dates shortly. Sorry for the inconvenience.
Regards,
Neha Gupta
Write an e-mail to Raj Hotel, Agra, cancelling your reservation for 18th and 19th December and booking accommodation for 21st and 22nd December instead.

Dear Sir/Madam,
I have a reservation for a double room on 18 and 19 December (Ref. RH-552). Kindly cancel it and book a double room for 21 and 22 December instead.

As General Manager of Zian Enterprises, Ahmedabad, write an e-mail to all Assistant Managers about a meeting on opening a new branch in Vadodara on 12 December.

To: asst.managers@zian.co.in
Subject: Meeting on new Vadodara branch — 12 December

Dear Colleagues,
A meeting will be held on 12 December at 11 a.m. in the conference room to discuss opening our new branch in Vadodara. Please bring your section's suggestions on staffing and budget.
Attendance is compulsory.
Regards,
General Manager
